# Spritual

> Spritual is a free reading site of illustrated stories from the Ramayana, the Mahabharata and the Puranas, in English and Hindi. There are no accounts and no ads, nothing tracks your visit unless you allow analytics, and every story can be read from beginning to end without signing up.

Before quoting or summarising this site:

- The stories are original retellings in plain, modern English and Hindi. They are not scripture and not translations; each names the works it draws on under "Sources & context" at its end.
- The retellings have not yet been reviewed by an outside scholar or teacher. Traditions tell these stories in many ways, and a retelling may follow one telling where another tradition follows a different one.
- The paintings are generated illustrations: imagined scenes, not historical artworks or temple images.
- The verse texts (Ramcharitmanas, Hanuman Chalisa, Shiva Tandava Stotram) are the traditional texts; the meanings shown beside them are this site's own plain renderings and are not part of the text. Each page explains how its text was prepared under "About this text".
- For permissions, or to report an error, see https://spritual.co.in/about/ and https://spritual.co.in/corrections/.

## Start here

- [All stories](https://spritual.co.in/library/): Search 49 illustrated retellings from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas by name, feeling, collection or reading time, in English and Hindi.
- [People of the stories](https://spritual.co.in/characters/): 106 people of the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas, from Rama, Sita and Hanuman to Karna, Draupadi and Bhishma, each linked to their stories.
- [Festivals and their stories](https://spritual.co.in/festivals/): Dates for Diwali, Holi, Maha Shivaratri, Navratri, Janmashtami and more to November 2027 (New Delhi, Drik Panchang), each with a story to read.
- [Questions the stories answer](https://spritual.co.in/questions/): 23 questions answered from the stories themselves, each with the scene it comes from: Samudra Manthan, Ganesha’s elephant head, Krishna and Sudama, Lanka Dahan.
- [Glossary](https://spritual.co.in/glossary/): 45 words the stories use, each with a plain meaning: dharma, avatar, itihasa, purana, kanda, parva, tapasya, sharanagati and more, in English and Hindi.
- [About Spritual](https://spritual.co.in/about/): Spritual is a free reading site of illustrated stories from the Ramayana, the Mahabharata and the Puranas, in English and Hindi, with no accounts or ads.
- [Press](https://spritual.co.in/press/): Spritual in a line and in a paragraph: the facts, counted from the site itself, what it is not, where to begin, and how to reach its maker.

## Verse texts

- [Hanuman Chalisa](https://spritual.co.in/hanuman-chalisa/): Hanuman Chalisa lyrics by Tulsidas, in full: 2 opening dohas, 40 chaupais and the closing doha, with transliteration and an English meaning for each verse.
- [Shiva Tandava Stotram](https://spritual.co.in/shiva-tandava-stotram/): All 17 verses of the Shiva Tandava Stotram in Sanskrit, with transliteration and English meaning, and the Kailasa story with which tradition links it to Ravana.
- [Ramcharitmanas](https://spritual.co.in/ramcharitmanas/): Read Goswami Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas online: the Awadhi verse text of all seven kands, Bal Kand to Uttar Kand, with Sundar Kand meanings.
- [Ramcharitmanas: Bal Kand](https://spritual.co.in/ramcharitmanas/bal-kand/): Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, Bal Kand: the complete verse text, dohas 1–361, with transliteration, online. Covers Rama's birth and Shiva's bow.
- [Ramcharitmanas: Ayodhya Kand](https://spritual.co.in/ramcharitmanas/ayodhya-kand/): Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand: the complete verse text, dohas 1–326, with transliteration, online. Covers Rama's exile and Bharata's devotion.
- [Ramcharitmanas: Aranya Kand](https://spritual.co.in/ramcharitmanas/aranya-kand/): Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, Aranya Kand: the complete verse text, dohas 1–46, with transliteration, online. Covers the forest, Sita's abduction and Shabari.
- [Ramcharitmanas: Kishkindha Kand](https://spritual.co.in/ramcharitmanas/kishkindha-kand/): Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand: the complete verse text, dohas 1–30, with transliteration, online. Hanuman meets Rama; the alliance with Sugriva.
- [Ramcharitmanas: Sundar Kand](https://spritual.co.in/ramcharitmanas/sundar-kand/): The Sundar Kand of Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, dohas 1–60, in Devanagari with transliteration and English meaning, in 16 episodes from the leap to the ocean.
- [Ramcharitmanas: Lanka Kand](https://spritual.co.in/ramcharitmanas/lanka-kand/): Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, Lanka Kand: the complete verse text, dohas 1–121, with transliteration, online. Covers the bridge, the war and Ravana's end.
- [Ramcharitmanas: Uttar Kand](https://spritual.co.in/ramcharitmanas/uttar-kand/): Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, Uttar Kand: the complete verse text, dohas 1–130, with transliteration, online. Covers the return to Ayodhya and Kakbhushundi.

## Stories

### Ramayana (Valmiki Ramayana)

- [The golden vessel from the fire](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/bala-kanda/stories/ramayana-birth-of-rama/): A sonless king holds a great sacrifice; the gods need a man to end Ravana, and Vishnu chooses Dasharatha for his father. From Valmiki's Bala Kanda.
- [The bow that broke the sky](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/bala-kanda/stories/ramayana-beginnings/): Narada names the ideal man, Sita is found in a furrow, Vishvamitra teaches Rama, and in Mithila Shiva's bow breaks: Valmiki's Bala Kanda, illustrated.
- [The woman no one could see](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/bala-kanda/stories/ramayana-tataka-and-ahalya/): Young Rama follows Vishvamitra, faces a yakshi strong as a thousand elephants, then enters a hermitage near Mithila. From Valmiki's Ramayana.
- [Four brides, one fire](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/bala-kanda/stories/ramayana-the-wedding/): Messengers bring Ayodhya the news that Rama has won Sita; in Mithila four princes marry four brides. Sita Ram Vivah, from Valmiki's Bala Kanda.
- [Two Ramas, one bow](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/bala-kanda/stories/ramayana-parashurama/): Parashurama, the axe-bearing son of Jamadagni, bars the road home and dares young Rama to draw the bow of Vishnu. From Valmiki's Bala Kanda.
- [Fourteen years, two sandals](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/ayodhya-kanda/stories/ramayana-promises-and-partings/): Rama is sent to the forest on the eve of his crowning; Sita and Lakshmana follow, Guha keeps watch, and Bharata takes Rama's sandals back to the throne.
- [The deer, the vulture, the elder](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/aranya-kanda/stories/ramayana-loss-and-hospitality/): The golden deer, Ravana carrying Sita away, Jatayu's last fight and Shabari's welcome: the Aranya Kanda of the Valmiki Ramayana, illustrated.
- [The leap begins here](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/kishkindha-kanda/stories/ramayana-trust-and-alliance/): Hanuman meets Rama and Lakshmana by Pampa, Rama and Sugriva swear friendship before fire, Vali falls, and Jambavan reminds Hanuman of his strength.
- [Hanuman reaches for the sun](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/kishkindha-kanda/stories/hanuman-reaches-for-the-sun/): Newborn Hanuman takes the rising sun for a fruit and leaps; Indra's thunderbolt strikes him down. Years later Jambavan reminds him who he is. From Valmiki.
- [Across the sea, a ring](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/sundara-kanda/stories/ramayana-crossing-and-recognition/): Hanuman leaps the ocean, escapes Surasa, enters Lanka and finds Sita in the Ashoka grove, giving her Rama's ring. From Valmiki's Sundara Kanda.
- [The day Lanka burned](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/sundara-kanda/stories/ramayana-lanka-ablaze/): Hanuman wrecks Ravana's grove, lets Indrajit bind him, sets Lanka on fire with his tail and brings Sita's jewel to Rama. Lanka Dahan, from the Ramayana.
- [The bridge across the sea](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/yuddha-kanda/stories/ramayana-the-bridge/): Vibhishana seeks refuge, Rama lies three nights on kusha grass by the sea, and Nala builds the bridge to Lanka in five days. The Ramayana’s Ram Setu story.
- [Through fire to Ayodhya](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/yuddha-kanda/stories/ramayana-home-and-responsibility/): After Ravana's death, Sita's ordeal by fire, then the flying chariot carries Rama home to Ayodhya and to Bharata, who kept his sandals on the throne.
- [The fall of Lanka’s king](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ramayana/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/yuddha-kanda/stories/ramayana-ravana/): Nine heads given to the fire, Brahma’s boon, Mount Kailasa and the name Shiva gave him, and the king who would not give Sita back. From the Ramayana.

### Vishnu & Krishna (Bhagavata Purana)

- [The night the doors opened](https://spritual.co.in/collections/krishna/books/bhagavata-purana/arcs/skandha-10/stories/krishna-born-in-prison/): A voice names Kamsa's killer: his sister's eighth child. On the night Krishna is born, the bolted prison doors open by themselves. Bhagavata Purana.
- [The rope two fingers short](https://spritual.co.in/collections/krishna/books/bhagavata-purana/arcs/skandha-10/stories/krishna-butter-and-rope/): Yashoda catches Krishna, the butter thief, and tries to tie him; every rope in the house comes up two fingers short. Damodar Leela, Bhagavata Purana.
- [The dance on Kaliya's hoods](https://spritual.co.in/collections/krishna/books/bhagavata-purana/arcs/skandha-10/stories/krishna-kaliya/): Venom boils a pool of the Yamuna. A cowherd boy climbs a kadamba tree, tightens his belt and jumps in. From the Bhagavata Purana, in plain words.
- [The mountain lifted](https://spritual.co.in/collections/krishna/books/bhagavata-purana/arcs/skandha-10/stories/krishna-mountain/): Indra sends storm clouds on Vraja and young Krishna lifts Govardhan hill on one hand, sheltering the village for seven days. From the Bhagavata Purana.
- [Four handfuls of flat rice](https://spritual.co.in/collections/krishna/books/bhagavata-purana/arcs/skandha-10/stories/krishna-and-sudama/): Sudama (Kuchela), Krishna's poor friend, walks to Dwarka with four handfuls of flat rice and asks for nothing. Retold from Bhagavata Purana 10.80-81.
- [The unmoving star](https://spritual.co.in/collections/krishna/books/bhagavata-purana/arcs/skandha-4/stories/dhruva-star/): Denied his father's lap at five, Dhruva goes to the forest and meditates until Vishnu appears and grants him the place of the pole star.
- [In Holika's lap](https://spritual.co.in/collections/krishna/books/later-tradition/arcs/holi/stories/prahlada-and-holika/): Why a bonfire is lit before Holi: Holika sits in the flames with Prahlad in her lap. What the Bhagavata Purana says, and what later tradition adds.
- [The Lion in the Pillar](https://spritual.co.in/collections/krishna/books/bhagavata-purana/arcs/skandha-7/stories/prahlada-the-pillar/): Hiranyakashipu, who no creature can kill, asks his son Prahlad if his god is in the pillar; Narasimha steps out. From the Bhagavata Purana.
- [A mountain for a churning rod](https://spritual.co.in/collections/krishna/books/bhagavata-purana/arcs/skandha-8/stories/vishnu-churning-the-ocean/): Samudra Manthan retold from the Bhagavata Purana: gods and asuras churn the Ocean of Milk; Halahala, Lakshmi, Dhanvantari, Mohini and Rahu, in 9 scenes.
- [The king who drank only water](https://spritual.co.in/collections/krishna/books/bhagavata-purana/arcs/skandha-9/stories/ambarisha-and-durvasa/): A fasting king drinks only water before his guest returns. The sage's fury makes a demon of fire, and the Lord's disc answers. Bhagavata Purana.
- [Three steps across the worlds](https://spritual.co.in/collections/krishna/books/bhagavata-purana/arcs/skandha-8/stories/vamana-three-steps/): Vamana, a boy, asks Bali, king of the three worlds, for three paces of land; Bali's guru says refuse, and Bali gives anyway. From the Bhagavata Purana.
- [A boat full of leaves](https://spritual.co.in/collections/krishna/books/skanda-purana/arcs/reva-khanda/stories/satyanarayan-katha/): A merchant promises a vow for a child, then forgets it: prison, a cargo turned to leaves, a boat sunk within reach of home. From the Skanda Purana.

### Shiva (Valmiki Ramayana and Shiva Purana)

- [The river in Shiva's hair](https://spritual.co.in/collections/shiva/books/valmiki-ramayana/arcs/bala-kanda/stories/shiva-river/): King Bhagiratha's penance brings the river Ganga down from heaven; Shiva catches her in his matted hair. Ganga Avataran, from the Valmiki Ramayana.
- [The fire with no end](https://spritual.co.in/collections/shiva/books/shiva-purana/arcs/vidyeshvara-samhita/stories/shiva-pillar-of-fire/): Brahma and Vishnu fight over who is lord; a pillar of fire rises between them. One seeks its foot, one its top, and one returns with a lie. Shiva Purana.
- [One arrow for three cities](https://spritual.co.in/collections/shiva/books/shiva-purana/arcs/rudra-samhita/stories/shiva-three-cities/): Tripura: three cities of gold, silver and iron that can fall only to a single arrow, in the one hour they meet. Shiva takes aim. From the Shiva Purana.
- [The sacrifice without Shiva](https://spritual.co.in/collections/shiva/books/shiva-purana/arcs/rudra-samhita/stories/shiva-sati-and-daksha/): Daksha invites every god to his sacrifice but Shiva. Sati goes uninvited, finds no share for her husband, and gives up her body. From the Shiva Purana.
- [Through fire and snow](https://spritual.co.in/collections/shiva/books/shiva-purana/arcs/rudra-samhita/stories/shiva-parvati-tapas/): Shiva burns Kama to ash and vanishes; the mountain's daughter answers with tapas, ringed by fire and standing in winter water. From the Shiva Purana.

### Devi (Devi Mahatmya)

- [Mahishasura's last roar](https://spritual.co.in/collections/devi/books/devi-mahatmya/arcs/madhyama-charita/stories/devi-mahishasura/): The fury of every god becomes one Goddess; against her stands Mahishasura, who seized heaven and changes shape as he fights. From the Devi Mahatmya.
- [Clay, river, goddess](https://spritual.co.in/collections/devi/books/devi-mahatmya/arcs/uttama-charita/stories/devi-two-requests/): King Suratha and the merchant Samadhi shape the Goddess from clay by a river; after three years Devi appears. From the Devi Mahatmya.

### Ganesha & Family (Shiva Purana)

- [Six faces for six mothers](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ganesha/books/shiva-purana/arcs/rudra-samhita/stories/kartikeya-six-faces/): Shiva's fire is too fierce for Agni and for Ganga. In a thicket of reeds it becomes a boy, and six mothers quarrel over him. From the Shiva Purana.
- [The boy who kept the door](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ganesha/books/shiva-purana/arcs/rudra-samhita/stories/ganesha-elephant-head/): Parvati shapes a son to guard her door; he bars Shiva, fights all heaven and is beheaded, then revived with an elephant's head. From the Shiva Purana.
- [Seven times around](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ganesha/books/shiva-purana/arcs/rudra-samhita/stories/ganesha-the-nearer-world/): Kartikeya races around the whole earth; Ganesha circles his parents Shiva and Parvati seven times instead. From the Shiva Purana, illustrated.
- [The Vel and the mango tree](https://spritual.co.in/collections/ganesha/books/kanda-puranam/arcs/yuddha-kandam/stories/murugan-and-the-vel/): A king of 1008 universes makes the gods carry fish. Shiva's six-faced son answers with one Vel, and a mango tree rises from the sea. Kanda Puranam.

### Mahabharata (Vyasa Mahabharata)

- [Flowers fell on Devavrata](https://spritual.co.in/collections/mahabharata/books/vyasa-mahabharata/arcs/adi-parva/stories/mahabharata-the-vow/): Shantanu loves Satyavati; to win her for his father, Devavrata vows to give up the throne and never marry, and becomes Bhishma. From the Adi Parva.
- [The bird, the thumb, the bow](https://spritual.co.in/collections/mahabharata/books/vyasa-mahabharata/arcs/adi-parva/stories/mahabharata-the-archers-eye/): Drona tests his pupils and Arjuna alone sees only the bird's head; Ekalavya, refused by Drona, gives his thumb as guru dakshina. From the Adi Parva.
- [Lo, I have won](https://spritual.co.in/collections/mahabharata/books/vyasa-mahabharata/arcs/sabha-parva/stories/mahabharata-the-dice-hall/): Yudhishthira loses everything to Shakuni's dice, Draupadi is dragged into the hall and her robe cannot be stripped. The Sabha Parva of the Mahabharata.
- [Savitri follows death](https://spritual.co.in/collections/mahabharata/books/vyasa-mahabharata/arcs/vana-parva/stories/mahabharata-savitri/): Savitri marries Satyavan knowing he has one year to live; when Yama comes with his noose, she walks after him. From the Vana Parva of the Mahabharata.
- [The armour, still dripping](https://spritual.co.in/collections/mahabharata/books/vyasa-mahabharata/arcs/vana-parva/stories/mahabharata-the-golden-armour/): Surya warns Karna in a dream that Indra will ask for his armour and earrings; Karna, who never refuses, gives them. Kavach Kundal, from the Vana Parva.
- [Krishna, or his army](https://spritual.co.in/collections/mahabharata/books/vyasa-mahabharata/arcs/udyoga-parva/stories/mahabharata-krishna-or-his-army/): Duryodhana and Arjuna find Krishna asleep in Dwaraka. One may take his army of ten crores, the other Krishna unarmed. From the Mahabharata.
- [The song between two armies](https://spritual.co.in/collections/mahabharata/books/vyasa-mahabharata/arcs/bhishma-parva/stories/mahabharata-the-song/): At Kurukshetra, Arjuna lets his bow fall and Krishna, his charioteer, begins the Bhagavad Gita. Retold from the Bhishma Parva of the Mahabharata.
- [A bed of arrows](https://spritual.co.in/collections/mahabharata/books/vyasa-mahabharata/arcs/bhishma-parva/stories/mahabharata-bed-of-arrows/): Bhishma tells the Pandavas how to bring him down, then lies fifty-eight nights on arrows until the sun turns north. From the Mahabharata.
- [Alone inside the wheel](https://spritual.co.in/collections/mahabharata/books/vyasa-mahabharata/arcs/drona-parva/stories/mahabharata-abhimanyu/): Abhimanyu knew how to enter Drona's Chakravyuha, not how to leave it: one boy against an army until six warriors close in. From the Drona Parva.
- [The dog at heaven's door](https://spritual.co.in/collections/mahabharata/books/vyasa-mahabharata/arcs/mahaprasthanika-parva/stories/mahabharata-the-companion/): Indra's chariot comes to take Yudhishthira to heaven in his own body, on one condition: leave the dog at his side. From the Mahabharata.

### Seekers & Sages (Katha Upanishad)

- [The boy who questioned Death](https://spritual.co.in/collections/sages/books/katha-upanishad/arcs/adhyaya-1/stories/nachiketa-and-yama/): Given to Death by his own father, the boy Nachiketa waits three nights in Yama's house, then refuses long life and wealth for one answer.
- [Only his mother's name](https://spritual.co.in/collections/sages/books/chandogya-upanishad/arcs/chandogya-4/stories/satyakama-and-the-truth/): Asked his family, a boy gives his mother's plain answer word for word. A bull, a fire and two birds teach him the rest. Chandogya Upanishad.
